question: Which blood vessel carries nutrient-rich blood straight from the intestines to the liver?
explanation: You got this! The portal vein acts like a direct highway taking blood filled with digested nutrients straight from your gut to the liver for processing. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main job of hepatocytes inside the liver?

options.B: Handling metabolism and clearing out toxins
options.C: Pumping oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation

explanation: Hepatocytes are the hardworking main cells of the liver. They manage your metabolism, build proteins, and clear out body toxins every single day! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h1)

question: How is the Hepatitis A virus mainly spread from person to person?
explanation: Hepatitis A spreads easily when someone accidentally ingests food or water that has been contaminated with tiny amounts of infected stool. Good hand hygiene is key! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why do patients with viral hepatitis turn yellow (jaundice)?

options.A: Excessive production of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.B: Severe dehydration concentrating bile pigments in the skin
options.C: Damaged liver cells cannot process and clear out bilirubin
options.D: Direct bacterial infection of the superficial skin layers

explanation: When liver cells are inflamed, they struggle to process bilirubin properly. This yellow pigment builds up in the blood and skin, causing jaundice. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h2)

question: What major change happens to the liver tissue during cirrhosis?

options.B: Replacement of normal tissue with permanent scar tissue
options.D: Complete disappearance of the hepatic artery

explanation: Think of cirrhosis as chronic injury that causes the soft working tissue of the liver to turn into hard scar tissue (fibrosis). [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h3)

question: What causes swollen blood vessels (esophageal varices) in advanced liver cirrhosis?

options.A: High pressure in the portal vein forcing blood into smaller collateral vessels
options.B: Direct viral attack on the mucosal lining of the esophagus
options.C: Excessive stomach acid production rising into the upper airway
options.D: Swallowing sharp food particles that scrape the throat

explanation: When the scarred liver blocks blood flow, it causes a traffic jam called portal hypertension. Blood has to find other routes, swelling up fragile veins around the esophagus. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which waste product builds up in the blood to cause hepatic encephalopathy?
explanation: A healthy liver turns nitrogen waste like ammonia into safe urea. When the liver fails, ammonia builds up and affects brain function, causing confusion. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h4)

question: A nurse is checking a patient with early liver failure for brain confusion. Which physical sign should she look for?

options.A: Sudden paralysis of the lower extremities
options.B: Involuntary flapping tremor of the hands (asterixis)
options.C: Rigid muscle spasms in the jaw
options.D: Inability to focus the eyes on bright objects

explanation: Asterixis (often called a 'liver flap') is a classic sign where the patient holds their hands out, and the wrists briefly flap downward due to toxin buildup. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which blood test checks how well the liver is making proteins needed for blood clotting?
explanation: Spot on! Because the liver builds most of our clotting factors, testing how long blood takes to clot (PT/INR) shows us how well the liver is working. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h5)

question: What do high levels of AST and ALT on a blood test usually mean?

options.A: Rapid regeneration of healthy liver tissue
options.B: Active injury and damage to liver cells
options.C: An infection located within the urinary bladder

explanation: When liver cells get stressed or damaged, these internal enzymes (AST and ALT) leak out into the bloodstream like a distress signal. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h5)

question: How does the medicine lactulose help a patient with liver confusion (hepatic encephalopathy)?

options.A: By increasing blood pressure in the portal vein
options.B: By stimulating the liver to produce more albumin
options.C: By trapping ammonia in the gut and helping pass it out
options.D: By killing viruses attacking the liver cells

explanation: Lactulose makes the bowel acidic, trapping ammonia so the body can flush it out in the stool instead of letting it reach the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why are patients with swollen bellies (ascites) told to cut down on salt?

options.A: Salt makes the body hold onto water, worsening fluid in the belly
options.B: Sodium directly destroys liver cells if eaten in large amounts
options.C: Sodium prevents the body from absorbing water pills (diuretics)
options.D: High salt diets instantly trigger severe esophageal bleeding

explanation: Remember the golden rule: water follows salt! Keeping sodium low stops the kidneys from holding onto extra water, easing belly swelling. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h6)

question: A patient with severe liver disease is at high risk for bleeding. Which nursing care step is best?

options.A: Instructing the patient to use an electric razor for shaving
options.B: Giving all routine medications through deep muscle injections
options.C: Encouraging daily flossing with stiff-bristled dental tools
options.D: Applying firm pressure bandages to all minor skin sites

explanation: An electric razor prevents nicks and cuts. Since a failing liver struggles with clotting, we want to avoid any accidental bleeding! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why must patients with liver disease avoid taking casual painkillers like paracetamol without asking a doctor?

options.A: It neutralizes the effects of prescribed lactulose syrup
options.B: The liver has to process it, and it can cause more damage
options.C: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in liver patients
options.D: It increases the risk of dehydration and kidney failure

explanation: Medications like paracetamol are processed by the liver. When the liver is weak, these drugs can build up quickly and cause serious harm. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h7)
